brief.title: AI 简报｜Agent 控制面、工具调用评测与编程智能体训练
brief.overview: 本次简报依据提供的 5 条 arXiv 公告整理；这 5 篇均于 2026-10-19 公告，其中 1 篇首次提交于 2026-07-27，其余 4 篇首次提交于 2026-10-15，均早于公告日，不是当天首次发表的新论文。内容覆盖 MCP 工具调用控制、Agent 评测方法、编程/终端智能体训练与可验证推理。

items.title: Structured Authority Injection: Persistent Human Control for LLM Agents via Typed MCP Overrides
items.summary: 论文提出 Structured Authority Injection（SAI），把操作者的修正指令改为经类型化、schema 校验的 MCP 工具调用注入，而非自由文本覆盖；同时在每次提示前附加带优先级的“权威上下文”。SAI 定义 Constraint、Priority、Strategy 三类覆盖及其持久化语义，并通过规划进程不可访问的定向通道执行优先顺序。方法不需要微调、也不需要模型权重访问，适用于支持 MCP 工具调用的指令微调模型。在 9 个 LLM 与 8 个针对 Agent 失败模式的场景上，作者报告歧义指令解释减少、多轮规划中的权威衰减得到缓解，最强模型上提示开销最多降低 38%，但收益随模型与场景差异很大。该文首次提交于 2026-07-27，今日进入 arXiv 公告。
items.why_it_matters: 你关注工具调用且做后端，这套“把人工干预变成带 schema 的 MCP 调用”的做法可直接落在现有工具层：无需改模型，只需在编排器和权限通道上加约束，便于审计与回放。提示中的 38% 仅是特定模型/场景下的开销降幅，不代表通用提升。

items.title: Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution
items.summary: Harness-Delta Attribution（HDA）把“只改提示、工具与编排代码、不改权重”的 harness 进化收益拆成三部分：基准特定过拟合、测试时算力扩张、以及剩余可泛化部分的上界。作者在 11 个执行模型、3 个 harness 进化框架上覆盖数学、编程、创意与 Agent 任务；在 21 个搜索集提升统计显著的设置中，过拟合平均占收益 54%、测试时扩展占 14%，14 个设置中两者合计超过 50%。搜索集收益常无法迁移到留出任务，且仅靠验证集信号不足以阻止过拟合。论文首次提交于 2026-10-15。
items.why_it_matters: 你如果在调 prompt、工具描述或编排逻辑，这项结果说明“搜索集涨点”很可能只是过拟合加更多推理 token。可在内部评测中固定算力预算、保留真正留出的任务集，并要求报告收益归因，而不是只看单项基准分数。

items.title: Lean4AgenticRL: Advancing Agentic RL with Verifiable Multi-level Process Rewards
items.summary: Lean4AgenticRL 将 Agent 的多层过程奖励统一落到 Lean4 形式化 schema：除最终结果奖励外，还覆盖低层工具调用与中层工作流阶段，并用 workflow-stage-normalized GRPO 训练。作者据此训练 LAR-9B/27B 系列，LAR-27B 在 TerminalBench-2.1 上达到 77.3%；平均比基座模型高 9.89%，比其所知的同规模第二名模型高 5.07%。任务面向软件工程与通用终端操作。论文首次提交于 2026-10-15，今日进入公告，摘要未说明权重是否公开。
items.why_it_matters: 对做 AI 编程与终端 Agent 的后端工程师，关键是“工具调用级奖励”这一训练信号设计：如果你在做自建 Agent 或微调，可参考把一次任务的阶段与工具调用拆开计分，而不是只奖励最终通过。77.3% 是单一基准上的成绩，并非满分或跨任务通用能力。

items.title: PRIME: Towards Verifiable Evidence-Grounded Reasoning in LLM Agents
items.summary: PRIME 要求 Agent 在检查前先固定“证据路线”，说明每种结论可如何被证明；再由独立程序记录每次检查结果，拒绝证据不足以支持的结论，并提示或代跑可支撑更强结论的检查。在 480 个公共记录任务上，直接看到需求说明的 Agent 在 26.7% 的任务中给出了未经证实的结论，PRIME 为 0；其引导与补充检查把“有依据结论”的平均得分从仅会拒答时的 30.1 提高到 59.2（满分 100）。这些结果依赖三个条件：需求正确、检查点位置已知且精确、停止时预算充足。论文首次提交于 2026-10-15。
items.why_it_matters: 你关注工具调用，这类“规则+账本”模式可以直接实现为后端服务：把每条结论绑定到具体检查记录，缺证据就拒答。注意 0% 未经证实结论是在受控任务和已知检查点条件下得到的，真实系统里需求歧义与工具失败仍需额外处理。

items.title: Testing the Planning Claims of LLM-Based Agents against Formal Semantics
items.summary: 作者用隐藏 PDDL 模型作形式语义基准，检验 LLM Agent 的规划能力：任务用自然语言表述，但动作是否可执行、目标是否达成、问题是否有解由 PDDL 判定。实验覆盖 5 个领域（含 2 个新领域，随论文发布）、4 个模型、6 种提示策略、3 种 Agent 架构。最佳配置在可解任务上离线求解 78%，在线仅 40%，在线时 Agent 多数未检查状态就行动；无解任务识别率不足 10%；更重的提示策略消耗为直接提示的 5 至 22 倍 token，却无明显收益。性能在模型间的差异大于提示策略或架构间的差异。论文首次提交于 2026-10-15。
items.why_it_matters: 这给“Agent 会规划”的说法提供了反例：端到端成功率和 LLM 评审都不等于可验证的行动轨迹。若你在做工具调用循环，应记录并校验每一步前置条件与状态读取，并优先换更强模型而非堆叠提示技巧。

evidence_quotes: We propose Structured Authority Injection (SAI), a protocol that addresses these issues by routing operator corrections through typed, schema-validated Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool calls and maintaining a ranked authority context prepended to each LLM prompt.

SAI defines three override classes (Constraint, Priority, and Strategy) with distinct persistence semantics and an explicit precedence order enforced via a directed authority channel inaccessible to the planning process.

evidence_quotes: Harness evolution automatically optimizes the prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration code around a fixed-weight model, offering a way to improve agentic systems without updating model weights.

We apply HDA to 11 executor models and three harness-evolution frameworks across math, coding, creativity, and agentic tasks. In 21 of these settings that show statistically significant search-set gains, we find that a large share of the improvement is explained by overfitting or test-time scaling.
Specifically, among these 21 settings, overfitting and test-time scaling account for 54% and 14% of the gain on average; their combined share exceeds 50% in 14 settings.

Using **Lean4AgenticRL**, we train **LAR-9B/27B**, a family of models with enhanced agentic capability. On average, our models outperform the base model by **9.89%** and surpass the second-best model of comparable size we know by **5.07%**.

evidence_quotes: Tasks are posed in natural language, but each is grounded in a hidden PDDL model that decides whether every action is applicable, whether the goal is reached, and whether a plan exists at all.

Across five domains (two of them new, all released with the paper), four models, six prompting strategies and three agent architectures, the best configuration solves 78% of the solvable tasks offline but only 40% online, where agents mostly act without inspecting the state.

Unsolvable tasks are recognised in under 10% of episodes, and heavier prompting strategies use 5 to 22 times as many tokens as direct prompting with no clear gain. In our experiments, planning performance varied more across models than across prompting strategies or agent architectures.

We propose Structured Authority Injection (SAI), a protocol that addresses these issues by routing operator corrections through typed, schema-validated Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool calls and maintaining a ranked authority context prepended to each LLM prompt. Evaluation across nine LLMs and eight scenarios targeting agent failure modes shows reduced ambiguous directive interpretation and mitigated authority decay across planning iterations, with lower prompt overhead in the strongest models (up to 38% depending on model and scenario), though benefit varies substantially across models. {"id": "a97c1f5a709e4de6f7ba", "title": "Lean4AgenticRL: Advancing Agentic RL with Verifiable Multi-level Process Rewards", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22448", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-15T15:26:54+00:00", "first_published_at": "2026-10-15T15:26:54+00:00", "announced_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "updated_at": null, "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "time_basis": "feed_announcement", "text": "Abstract: Enhancing the agentic capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) to tackle complex software engineering (SWE) and general terminal-usage problems is a pressing challenge. Current state-of-the-art LLMs often go through large-scale agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL). However, they mostly rely on high-level outcome rewards, with minimal consideration of low-level toolcall and mid-level workflow-stage rewards, which makes the training less effective. To overcome this limitation, we propose **Lean4AgenticRL**, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first framework that grounds multi-level process rewards in the unified Lean4 formalization schema for open-ended agentic RL. **Lean4AgenticRL** first builds a *problem-specific workflow* system that balances the agent's own capability and controllability during execution, laying the foundation for further verification. Subsequently, our workflow formalization and multi-level reward annotation methods enable agent behavior verification within a general harness system. It provides multi-level rewards to support more effective agentic RL with the workflow-stage-normalized GRPO algorithm. Using **Lean4AgenticRL**, we train **LAR-9B/27B**, a family of models with enhanced agentic capability. Extensive experiments indicate that our model outperforms the leading model of similar size. **LAR-27B** achieves **77.3%** on TerminalBench-2.1. On average, our models outperform the base model by **9.89%** and surpass the second-best model of comparable size we know by **5.07%**. These results indicate the potential of integrating formal methods in enhancing open-ended agentic RL.", "evidence_kind": "abstract", "demo": false, "publication_kind": "preprint"}

{"id": "f34ad45741b405ff9e69", "title": "Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22466", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-15T17:39:38+00:00", "first_published_at": "2026-10-15T17:39:38+00:00", "announced_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "updated_at": null, "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "time_basis": "feed_announcement", "text": "Abstract: Harness evolution automatically optimizes the prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration code around a fixed-weight model, offering a way to improve agentic systems without updating model weights. The agent harness is iteratively optimized to achieve higher performance on the search set. But how much of this gain reflects benchmark-specific overfitting or additional inference-time compute, and how much may generalize beyond the search set? We apply HDA to 11 executor models and three harness-evolution frameworks across math, coding, creativity, and agentic tasks. In 21 of these settings that show statistically significant search-set gains, we find that a large share of the improvement is explained by overfitting or test-time scaling. Specifically, among these 21 settings, overfitting and test-time scaling account for 54% and 14% of the gain on average; their combined share exceeds 50% in 14 settings. The residual and held-out transfer vary substantially across tasks, models, and frameworks. Importantly, search-set gains often fail to transfer to held-out tasks, and provide limited evidence that they will persist under practical distribution shifts. Moreover, validation-based signals are insufficient to prevent overfitting. These results motivate attribution-aware evaluation in future harness evolution research.", "evidence_kind": "abstract", "demo": false, "publication_kind": "preprint"}

{"id": "8cad1d7071d358947cb2", "title": "Testing the Planning Claims of LLM-Based Agents against Formal Semantics", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22469", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-15T17:47:30+00:00", "first_published_at": "2026-10-15T17:47:30+00:00", "announced_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "updated_at": null, "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "time_basis": "feed_announcement", "text": "Abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly credited with the competences of practical reasoning: planning, monitoring, and correcting their own actions. Their success is attributed to the prompting strategies and agent architectures built around the model, such as chain-of-thought, search-based prompting, self-refinement, reflection, critics and tool-using loops. Yet these claims are usually supported by end-to-end success rates, which show only whether a task was completed, or by LLM judges, which are not verifiers. We test LLM planning against formal semantics. Tasks are posed in natural language, but each is grounded in a hidden PDDL model that decides whether every action is applicable, whether the goal is reached, and whether a plan exists at all. arguments.overview: 过去 24 小时 OpenAI、Hugging Face、Google AI 三个源均无条目；TechCrunch 仅两条公司股权与人员交易类新闻，按“融资/交易”偏好排除。可用的相关信息集中在 arXiv 今日公告中（共 40 条），以下 5 篇均于今日公告但首次提交早于今日，不是今天首次发表的新论文。选取方向覆盖 MCP 工具调用控制、Agent 评测方法、编程/终端智能体训练与可验证推理，贴合后端工程与 Agent 工程实践。
selections: article_id='da92b80397690dde35e8' summary='论文提出 Structured Authority Injection（SAI），把操作者的修正指令改为经类型化、schema 校验的 MCP 工具调用注入，而非自由文本覆盖；同时在每次提示前附加带优先级的“权威上下文”。SAI 定义 Constraint、Priority、Strategy 三类覆盖及其持久化语义，并通过规划进程不可访问的定向通道执行优先顺序。方法不需要微调、也不需要模型权重访问，适用于支持 MCP 工具调用的指令微调模型。在 9 个 LLM 与 8 个针对 Agent 失败模式的场景上，作者报告歧义指令解释减少、多轮规划中的权威衰减得到缓解，最强模型上提示开销最多降低 38%，但收益随模型与场景差异很大。该文首次提交于 2026-07-27，今日进入 arXiv 公告。' why_it_matters='你关注工具调用且做后端，这套“把人工干预变成带 schema 的 MCP 调用”的做法可直接落在现有工具层：无需改模型，只需在编排器和权限通道上加约束，便于审计与回放。提示中的 38% 仅是特定模型/场景下的开销降幅，不代表通用提升。' topic='Agent / 工具调用' relevance=3

article_id='f34ad45741b405ff9e69' summary='Harness-Delta Attribution（HDA）把“只改提示、工具与编排代码、不改权重”的 harness 进化收益拆成三部分：基准特定过拟合、测试时算力扩张、以及剩余可泛化部分的上界。作者在 11 个执行模型、3 个 harness 进化框架上覆盖数学、编程、创意与 Agent 任务；在 21 个搜索集提升统计显著的设置中，过拟合平均占收益 54%、测试时扩展占 14%，14 个设置中两者合计超过 50%。搜索集收益常无法迁移到留出任务，且仅靠验证集信号不足以阻止过拟合。论文首次提交于 2026-10-15。' why_it_matters='你如果在调 prompt、工具描述或编排逻辑，这项结果说明“搜索集涨点”很可能只是过拟合加更多推理 token。可在内部评测中固定算力预算、保留真正留出的任务集，并要求报告收益归因，而不是只看单项基准分数。' topic='AI 编程 / Agent 评测' relevance=3

article_id='a97c1f5a709e4de6f7ba' summary='Lean4AgenticRL 将 Agent 的多层过程奖励统一落到 Lean4 形式化 schema：除最终结果奖励外，还覆盖低层工具调用与中层工作流阶段，并用 workflow-stage-normalized GRPO 训练。作者据此训练 LAR-9B/27B 系列，LAR-27B 在 TerminalBench-2.1 上达到 77.3%；平均比基座模型高 9.89%，比其所知的同规模第二名模型高 5.07%。任务面向软件工程与通用终端操作。论文首次提交于 2026-10-15，今日进入公告，摘要未说明权重是否公开。' why_it_matters='对做 AI 编程与终端 Agent 的后端工程师，关键是“工具调用级奖励”这一训练信号设计：如果你在做自建 Agent 或微调，可参考把一次任务的阶段与工具调用拆开计分，而不是只奖励最终通过。77.3% 是单一基准上的成绩，并非满分或跨任务通用能力。' topic='AI 编程 / Agent 训练' relevance=3

article_id='434246a93fec15537b14' summary='PRIME 要求 Agent 在检查前先固定“证据路线”，说明每种结论可如何被证明；再由独立程序记录每次检查结果，拒绝证据不足以支持的结论，并提示或代跑可支撑更强结论的检查。在 480 个公共记录任务上，直接看到需求说明的 Agent 在 26.7% 的任务中给出了未经证实的结论，PRIME 为 0；其引导与补充检查把“有依据结论”的平均得分从仅会拒答时的 30.1 提高到 59.2（满分 100）。这些结果依赖三个条件：需求正确、检查点位置已知且精确、停止时预算充足。论文首次提交于 2026-10-15。' why_it_matters='你关注工具调用，这类“规则+账本”模式可以直接实现为后端服务：把每条结论绑定到具体检查记录，缺证据就拒答。注意 0% 未经证实结论是在受控任务和已知检查点条件下得到的，真实系统里需求歧义与工具失败仍需额外处理。' topic='Agent / 可验证推理' relevance=2

selected_evidence.title: PRIME: Towards Verifiable Evidence-Grounded Reasoning in LLM Agents
selected_evidence.text: Abstract: LLM agents are used to check records against an organization's requirements, for example whether a vulnerability report is ready for investigation. Requirements often allow several ways to be met, such as a severity rating with a curator-reviewed advisory or a published advisory link. Agents fail by accepting a report after a required check has failed, or by settling for a weaker conclusion without trying another way that could still succeed. We introduce PRIME (Precommitted Rules for Inference from Minimal Evidence). Before checking, it fixes evidence routes specifying how each conclusion may be justified. A separate program records each check result and refuses any conclusion the results do not justify. It also points the agent to checks that could justify a stronger conclusion, or runs them itself. PRIME reports only conclusions authorized by its rules and ledger. With correct requirements, exact checks at known locations, and sufficient budget at stopping, completion reaches the strongest supported conclusion. On 480 public-record tasks, an agent shown the requirements reported unjustified conclusions on 26.7% of tasks, while PRIME reported none. Its directions and added checks raised the average score for justified conclusions from 30.1, with refusal alone, to the maximum of 59.2 out of 100.

selected_evidence.title: Testing the Planning Claims of LLM-Based Agents against Formal Semantics
selected_evidence.text: Abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly credited with the competences of practical reasoning: planning, monitoring, and correcting their own actions. Their success is attributed to the prompting strategies and agent architectures built around the model, such as chain-of-thought, search-based prompting, self-refinement, reflection, critics and tool-using loops. Yet these claims are usually supported by end-to-end success rates, which show only whether a task was completed, or by LLM judges, which are not verifiers. We test LLM planning against formal semantics. Tasks are posed in natural language, but each is grounded in a hidden PDDL model that decides whether every action is applicable, whether the goal is reached, and whether a plan exists at all. Across five domains (two of them new, all released with the paper), four models, six prompting strategies and three agent architectures, the best configuration solves 78% of the solvable tasks offline but only 40% online, where agents mostly act without inspecting the state. Unsolvable tasks are recognised in under 10% of episodes, and heavier prompting strategies use 5 to 22 times as many tokens as direct prompting with no clear gain. In our experiments, planning performance varied more across models than across prompting strategies or agent architectures. Claims that agents can plan require evidence from validated action traces.

selected_evidence.title: Lean4AgenticRL: Advancing Agentic RL with Verifiable Multi-level Process Rewards
selected_evidence.text: Abstract: Enhancing the agentic capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) to tackle complex software engineering (SWE) and general terminal-usage problems is a pressing challenge. Current state-of-the-art LLMs often go through large-scale agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL). However, they mostly rely on high-level outcome rewards, with minimal consideration of low-level toolcall and mid-level workflow-stage rewards, which makes the training less effective. To overcome this limitation, we propose **Lean4AgenticRL**, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first framework that grounds multi-level process rewards in the unified Lean4 formalization schema for open-ended agentic RL. **Lean4AgenticRL** first builds a *problem-specific workflow* system that balances the agent's own capability and controllability during execution, laying the foundation for further verification. Subsequently, our workflow formalization and multi-level reward annotation methods enable agent behavior verification within a general harness system. It provides multi-level rewards to support more effective agentic RL with the workflow-stage-normalized GRPO algorithm. Using **Lean4AgenticRL**, we train **LAR-9B/27B**, a family of models with enhanced agentic capability. Extensive experiments indicate that our model outperforms the leading model of similar size. **LAR-27B** achieves **77.3%** on TerminalBench-2.1. On average, our models outperform the base model by **9.89%** and surpass the second-best model of comparable size we know by **5.07%**. These results indicate the potential of integrating formal methods in enhancing open-ended agentic RL.

selected_evidence.title: Structured Authority Injection: Persistent Human Control for LLM Agents via Typed MCP Overrides
selected_evidence.text: Abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly used as autonomous orchestrators in distributed and multi-agent systems, yet a control gap remains: no protocol-level mechanism allows human operators to inject binding directives that persist across planning cycles. Free-text overrides suffer from ambiguous interpretation due to lack of schema validation and from authority erosion as operator instructions lose influence within accumulating context. We propose Structured Authority Injection (SAI), a protocol that addresses these issues by routing operator corrections through typed, schema-validated Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool calls and maintaining a ranked authority context prepended to each LLM prompt. SAI defines three override classes (Constraint, Priority, and Strategy) with distinct persistence semantics and an explicit precedence order enforced via a directed authority channel inaccessible to the planning process. The method requires no model fine-tuning or access to model weights and applies to instruction-tuned LLMs supporting MCP tool use. Evaluation across nine LLMs and eight scenarios targeting agent failure modes shows reduced ambiguous directive interpretation and mitigated authority decay across planning iterations, with lower prompt overhead in the strongest models (up to 38% depending on model and scenario), though benefit varies substantially across models. SAI provides a general design pattern for agent systems requiring explicit and persistent human control.

selected_evidence.title: Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution
selected_evidence.text: Abstract: Harness evolution automatically optimizes the prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration code around a fixed-weight model, offering a way to improve agentic systems without updating model weights. The agent harness is iteratively optimized to achieve higher performance on the search set. But how much of this gain reflects benchmark-specific overfitting or additional inference-time compute, and how much may generalize beyond the search set? In this work, we introduce Harness-Delta Attribution (HDA), an evaluation protocol that dissects an evolution gain into artifact-driven overfitting, gains explained by test-time scaling, and the remainder, which gives an upper bound on residual generalizable improvement. We apply HDA to 11 executor models and three harness-evolution frameworks across math, coding, creativity, and agentic tasks. In 21 of these settings that show statistically significant search-set gains, we find that a large share of the improvement is explained by overfitting or test-time scaling. Specifically, among these 21 settings, overfitting and test-time scaling account for 54% and 14% of the gain on average; their combined share exceeds 50% in 14 settings. The residual and held-out transfer vary substantially across tasks, models, and frameworks. Importantly, search-set gains often fail to transfer to held-out tasks, and provide limited evidence that they will persist under practical distribution shifts. Moreover, validation-based signals are insufficient to prevent overfitting. These results motivate attribution-aware evaluation in future harness evolution research.

items.title: FRACTAL: A Self-Similar Multi-Agent Orchestration Architecture with Formal Communication, Convergence, and Depth Bounds
items.summary: FRACTAL 提出一种自相似的多智能体编排架构：同一套五组件模式（Orchestrator、Ensemble、Knowledge Ledger、Decision Maker、Meta-Observer）在分解树的每一层重复。形式化结论包括：在两阶段“盲提案/压力测试”协议下，节点内通信成本随集成规模与轮数线性增长（O(kr)，前提是评估者数量固定），自由辩论则为二次；用可测的多样性饱和阈值区分生成与评估阶段；在给定一致率下给出超多数收敛的概率界与分解深度界；层间升级用一次贝叶斯后验更新统一迟滞与契约违约信号。作者明确声明本文不报告定量性能结论，实证验证留待后续工作。首次提交于 2026-10-15。

evidence_quotes: We present an author-in-the-loop collaborative audit that makes author declarations explicit inputs to an AI agent's investigation and assessment.

The agent separately assesses whether results have been reproduced and whether authors need to provide clarification or make repairs, while human reviewers approve requests and decide whether concerns are resolved.

We deployed the system across 36 conference papers and 133 experimental tables and figures, raising 20 issues after human review. Further checks supported closing all the issues, although full reproduction remained unverified in some cases. We further compared repeated audits with complete and blank checklists to examine how author declarations shaped the agent's investigation and assessment.

We show how, when applied to simulation outputs such as nitrogen leaching, soil organic carbon variation, and yield predictions, it can deliver an interpretable, decision-oriented reading.", "evidence_kind": "feed_summary", "demo": false}, {"id": "434246a93fec15537b14", "title": "PRIME: Towards Verifiable Evidence-Grounded Reasoning in LLM Agents", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22426", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": null, "first_published_at": null, "announced_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "updated_at": null, "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "time_basis": "feed_announcement", "text": "arXiv:2610.22426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents are used to check records against an organization's requirements, for example whether a vulnerability report is ready for investigation. Its directions and added checks raised the average score for justified conclusions from 30.1, with refusal alone, to the maximum of 59.2 out of 100.", "evidence_kind": "feed_summary", "demo": false}, {"id": "c75b08a745837bc4fd9e", "title": "CGDT-CESN: Correlation-Guided and Dynamics-Trained Clustered Echo State Network for Multivariate Time-Series Prediction", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22430", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": null, "first_published_at": null, "announced_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "updated_at": null, "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "time_basis": "feed_announcement", "text": "arXiv:2610.22430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate prediction of multivariate time series requires models that simultaneously capture variable-specific dynamics and cross-variable interactions. {"id": "6ec636eceffcfb5999d5", "title": "Don't Retrain, Remix: Adaptation of Web Agents using Mixture Hypernetworks", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22539", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-15T18:37:41+00:00", "first_published_at": "2026-10-15T18:37:41+00:00", "announced_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "updated_at": null, "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "time_basis": "feed_announcement", "text": "Abstract: The web is not static or uniform. Websites that serve the same purpose can look and navigate very differently. Even within a single site, successive redesigns can change how familiar features are presented and accessed. Humans adapt to this by recognizing familiar interaction patterns and reusing what they already know. We give web agents a similar ability with WebMix, a mixture hypernetwork that adapts them to unseen interfaces by composing previously trained low-rank adapters. WebMix begins with a bank of adapters trained on source interfaces. At deployment, a scout agent explores the target interface and summarizes its observations into a compact manual. A lightweight router uses this manual to predict mixing coefficients over the adapter bank, which combine the existing adapters into a new one for inference. Adapting to a new interface takes only a scouting run and a forward pass, without gradient updates on the target. With Qwen and Llama models, we evaluate domain transfer on TimeWarp and WebArena-Lite-v2, and version transfer on TimeWarp. In all three settings, WebMix matches or outperforms in-context learning and LoRA baselines, often matching the average success of specialists trained directly on those interfaces. On TimeWarp domain transfer, it gains about 8 percentage points on average over the best baseline with both models. These gains do not come at the cost of seen interfaces, where WebMix keeps its lead, and extend to version transfer. Adapting to a new interface can therefore rely on exploration and composition instead of retraining.", "evidence_kind": "abstract", "demo": false, "publication_kind": "preprint"}

{"id": "bf13a92368f50af68cba", "title": "Repairing LLM-Generated Specifications with Deterministic Diagnosis", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22568", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-15T19:12:54+00:00", "first_published_at": "2026-10-15T19:12:54+00:00", "announced_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "updated_at": null, "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "time_basis": "feed_announcement", "text": "Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as formalizers: given a reasoning problem expressed in natural language, they produce a formal specification that a symbolic solver can then solve, with guarantees relative to that specification. Many specifications are runnable yet semantically wrong, encoding incorrect constraints, domains, objectives, predicates, or goals, and solver-error feedback dries up once execution succeeds. Purely LLM-based diagnosis, lacking a formal ground truth, often fails to spot these errors, and its ungrounded critiques cause regressions in 11.8% of initially correct specifications in our experiments. We propose DRAGO, a repair framework that replaces this ungrounded critique with deterministic, formalism-specific diagnosis, and retains a rewrite only when the diagnosed error weight strictly decreases under a reference-free acceptance predicate. Across five benchmarks spanning logical reasoning (SMT-LIB2), constraint programming (MiniZinc), and planning (PDDL), DRAGO cuts regressions by nearly an order of magnitude, to 1.3%, while improving answer accuracy by 12.9 percentage points over zero-shot formalization and 8.7 percentage points over LLM-diagnostic repair, averaged across benchmarks. We also uncover two rendering defects in Planetarium that cause 50% (3,086 instances) of its floor-tile split to be inconsistent with the reference formalizations, and release a corrected split.", "evidence_kind": "abstract", "demo": false, "publication_kind": "preprint"}

{"id": "051009ada2a4f647f6fc", "title": "On the SPOT: Enhancing Speculative Decoding for Diffusion Language Models via Commit-Order Prediction", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22543", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-15T18:40:42+00:00", "first_published_at": "2026-10-15T18:40:42+00:00", "announced_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "updated_at": null, "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "time_basis": "feed_announcement", "text": "Abstract: Diffusion language models (DLMs) promise parallel text generation, but in practice face an unresolved speed-quality trade-off. Exact decoding fills in only one masked position per model pass, while faster multi-token decoding schemes are lossy. Speculative decoding is the standard lossless acceleration for autoregressive models. However, it does not transfer directly to DLMs, which must choose both what to generate and where. We show that this order is the missing piece: the model's own predictions from the previous pass already give the right token at 92-100% of positions, but not which position comes next. Based on this observation, we introduce Speculating Positions Order Trajectory (SPOT), which learns to predict this order. A 0.62M-parameter model reads only the target's output distributions and proposes a tree of candidate continuations, and the target verifies all of them in a single pass by checking whether each equals its own next state. On the verification side, our analysis shows that prior block-diffusion verification approaches either assume $T=0$ or a sequential proposal interface. To support tree-based speculation at any temperature, we propose using coupled-noise match verification for diffusion blocks, following shared-Gumbel-noise coupling approaches. Our comprehensive experiments show that SPOT cuts target passes by up to 6.8x and reaches up to 3.2x the throughput of standard decoding, beating the calibrated and training-free drafting baselines in every task and budget at $T=0$ and $T=1$. In addition, we show that the learned drafter transfers across models, demonstrating successful transfer across six different DLMs. Project page: this https URL", "evidence_kind": "abstract", "demo": false, "publication_kind": "preprint"}

{"id": "7cc78127c883714f76f3", "title": "Author-in-the-loop Agentic Reproducibility Auditing for a Machine Learning Conference", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22465", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-15T17:28:51+00:00", "first_published_at": "2026-10-15T17:28:51+00:00", "announced_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "updated_at": null, "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "time_basis": "feed_announcement", "text": "Abstract: Reproducibility checks during peer review require a shared understanding of what authors' code is expected to reproduce. We present an author-in-the-loop collaborative audit that makes author declarations explicit inputs to an AI agent's investigation and assessment. A structured checklist records reproduction instructions and limitations; a two-stage workflow on GitHub connects agent checks to author clarification, revision, and agent reassessment. The agent separately assesses whether results have been reproduced and whether authors need to provide clarification or make repairs, while human reviewers approve requests and decide whether concerns are resolved. We deployed the system across 36 conference papers and 133 experimental tables and figures, raising 20 issues after human review. Further checks supported closing all the issues, although full reproduction remained unverified in some cases. We further compared repeated audits with complete and blank checklists to examine how author declarations shaped the agent's investigation and assessment. Our work contributes a collaborative workflow and agent design that use author knowledge to guide reproducibility auditing. The conference deployment provides empirical evidence that this approach can help identify and address reproducibility problems through collaboration among authors, agents, and reviewers.", "evidence_kind": "abstract", "demo": false, "publication_kind": "preprint"}

{"id": "bf28c7aa2007aa01571b", "title": "FRACTAL: A Self-Similar Multi-Agent Orchestration Architecture with Formal Communication, Convergence, and Depth Bounds", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22561", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-15T19:02:50+00:00", "first_published_at": "2026-10-15T19:02:50+00:00", "announced_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "updated_at": null, "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "time_basis": "feed_announcement", "text": "Abstract: We present FRACTAL, a self-similar multi-agent architecture for recursive goal decomposition, in which the same five-component organizational pattern -- Orchestrator, Ensemble, Knowledge Ledger, Decision Maker, Meta-Observer -- recurs at every level of a decomposition tree. We make four formal contributions: (1) a communication bound showing intra-node cost is linear in ensemble size and round count (O(kr)) under a two-phase blind-proposal/stress-test protocol, versus quadratic cost for free-form debate, with an explicit, stated assumption on fixed evaluator count; (2) a two-mode orchestration criterion separating generative and evaluative phases via a measurable diversity-saturation threshold; (3) a supermajority convergence guarantee with explicit probability bounds at stated agreement levels, and a formal depth bound under an operationalized goal-complexity measure; (4) a Bayesian inter-layer escalation mechanism unifying hysteresis and contract-breach signaling under one posterior update. We illustrate the architecture's execution qualitatively on a worked example and a multi-layer case study; we do not report quantitative performance claims in this paper, and we explicitly discuss the formal and inductive-bias limitations of the model, including an unimplemented but architecture-compatible direction toward bounded self-improvement. We use \"fractal\" as an architectural metaphor for self-similarity, not a measured mathematical property. Empirical validation of the architecture's comparative performance is left to future work.", "evidence_kind": "abstract", "demo": false, "publication_kind": "preprint"}

{"id": "5f9cc4741ffa08d59cab", "title": "From Natural Language Intent to Executable Control: Hierarchical Feedback-Guided LLM Planning for Multi-component Cyber-Physical Systems", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22441", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-15T14:52:57+00:00", "first_published_at": "2026-10-15T14:52:57+00:00", "announced_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "updated_at": null, "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "time_basis": "feed_announcement", "text": "Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) provide a convenient interface for translating natural language commands into task plans for cyber-physical systems (CPSs). However, two gaps hinder their use for real execution: generated plans may misinterpret or omit the user's intent, and even a logically plausible plan may be infeasible under component dynamics, interactions, or safety constraints. Existing LLM-based planning approaches often lack informative feedback on why a generated plan fails, providing little guidance for revising the plan accordingly. To address these challenges, we present a hierarchical feedback framework that uses different types of feedback information to guide LLMs in generating executable plans for CPSs. We prompt LLMs to generate both a structured task plan and corresponding signal temporal logic (STL) constraints, and design a sound algorithm that identifies definite contradictions between them and provides feedback for revising inconsistencies. At the execution level, when control synthesis fails, we extract different types of diagnostic information, such as violated constraints and conflicting component assignments, and feed them back to guide task replanning. Experiments on seven heterogeneous multi-component CPS scenarios have shown that our framework can generate executable plans and feasible control executions that satisfy the original natural language missions with a success rate of 87.9% with GPT-5.", "evidence_kind": "abstract", "demo": false, "publication_kind": "preprint"}

selections: article_id='6ec636eceffcfb5999d5' summary='WebMix 用混合超网络把已训练的低秩适配器组合成新适配器，让 Web Agent 适配未见界面时无需梯度更新：部署时先由 scout agent 探索目标界面并写成一份紧凑“手册”，轻量 router 据此预测 adapter bank 上的混合系数，合成后直接推理。作者用 Qwen 与 Llama 模型在 TimeWarp 的域迁移与版本迁移、以及 WebArena-Lite-v2 上评测，三种设置下与上下文学习、LoRA 基线持平或更优；TimeWarp 域迁移平均比最佳基线高约 8 个百分点，且在已见界面上保持领先、未见退化。论文首次提交于 2026-10-15，今日进入 arXiv 公告。' why_it_matters='把“适配新站点/新版本”从重新训练变成探索加组合，正好对应你接入内部系统时界面频繁改版的维护成本；不过证据只覆盖 Qwen/Llama 与三个基准，尚无真实生产流量下的延迟数据。' topic='Agent / 部署适配' relevance=3

selected_evidence.title: On the SPOT: Enhancing Speculative Decoding for Diffusion Language Models via Commit-Order Prediction
selected_evidence.text: Abstract: Diffusion language models (DLMs) promise parallel text generation, but in practice face an unresolved speed-quality trade-off. Exact decoding fills in only one masked position per model pass, while faster multi-token decoding schemes are lossy. Speculative decoding is the standard lossless acceleration for autoregressive models. However, it does not transfer directly to DLMs, which must choose both what to generate and where. We show that this order is the missing piece: the model's own predictions from the previous pass already give the right token at 92-100% of positions, but not which position comes next. Based on this observation, we introduce Speculating Positions Order Trajectory (SPOT), which learns to predict this order. A 0.62M-parameter model reads only the target's output distributions and proposes a tree of candidate continuations, and the target verifies all of them in a single pass by checking whether each equals its own next state. On the verification side, our analysis shows that prior block-diffusion verification approaches either assume $T=0$ or a sequential proposal interface. To support tree-based speculation at any temperature, we propose using coupled-noise match verification for diffusion blocks, following shared-Gumbel-noise coupling approaches. Our comprehensive experiments show that SPOT cuts target passes by up to 6.8x and reaches up to 3.2x the throughput of standard decoding, beating the calibrated and training-free drafting baselines in every task and budget at $T=0$ and $T=1$. In addition, we show that the learned drafter transfers across models, demonstrating successful transfer across six different DLMs. Project page: this https URL

selected_evidence.title: Don't Retrain, Remix: Adaptation of Web Agents using Mixture Hypernetworks
selected_evidence.text: Abstract: The web is not static or uniform. Websites that serve the same purpose can look and navigate very differently. Even within a single site, successive redesigns can change how familiar features are presented and accessed. Humans adapt to this by recognizing familiar interaction patterns and reusing what they already know. We give web agents a similar ability with WebMix, a mixture hypernetwork that adapts them to unseen interfaces by composing previously trained low-rank adapters. WebMix begins with a bank of adapters trained on source interfaces. At deployment, a scout agent explores the target interface and summarizes its observations into a compact manual. A lightweight router uses this manual to predict mixing coefficients over the adapter bank, which combine the existing adapters into a new one for inference. Adapting to a new interface takes only a scouting run and a forward pass, without gradient updates on the target. With Qwen and Llama models, we evaluate domain transfer on TimeWarp and WebArena-Lite-v2, and version transfer on TimeWarp. In all three settings, WebMix matches or outperforms in-context learning and LoRA baselines, often matching the average success of specialists trained directly on those interfaces. On TimeWarp domain transfer, it gains about 8 percentage points on average over the best baseline with both models. These gains do not come at the cost of seen interfaces, where WebMix keeps its lead, and extend to version transfer. Adapting to a new interface can therefore rely on exploration and composition instead of retraining.

selected_evidence.title: Author-in-the-loop Agentic Reproducibility Auditing for a Machine Learning Conference
selected_evidence.text: Abstract: Reproducibility checks during peer review require a shared understanding of what authors' code is expected to reproduce. We present an author-in-the-loop collaborative audit that makes author declarations explicit inputs to an AI agent's investigation and assessment. A structured checklist records reproduction instructions and limitations; a two-stage workflow on GitHub connects agent checks to author clarification, revision, and agent reassessment. The agent separately assesses whether results have been reproduced and whether authors need to provide clarification or make repairs, while human reviewers approve requests and decide whether concerns are resolved. We deployed the system across 36 conference papers and 133 experimental tables and figures, raising 20 issues after human review. Further checks supported closing all the issues, although full reproduction remained unverified in some cases. We further compared repeated audits with complete and blank checklists to examine how author declarations shaped the agent's investigation and assessment. Our work contributes a collaborative workflow and agent design that use author knowledge to guide reproducibility auditing. The conference deployment provides empirical evidence that this approach can help identify and address reproducibility problems through collaboration among authors, agents, and reviewers.

selected_evidence.title: Repairing LLM-Generated Specifications with Deterministic Diagnosis
selected_evidence.text: Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as formalizers: given a reasoning problem expressed in natural language, they produce a formal specification that a symbolic solver can then solve, with guarantees relative to that specification. Many specifications are runnable yet semantically wrong, encoding incorrect constraints, domains, objectives, predicates, or goals, and solver-error feedback dries up once execution succeeds. Purely LLM-based diagnosis, lacking a formal ground truth, often fails to spot these errors, and its ungrounded critiques cause regressions in 11.8% of initially correct specifications in our experiments. We propose DRAGO, a repair framework that replaces this ungrounded critique with deterministic, formalism-specific diagnosis, and retains a rewrite only when the diagnosed error weight strictly decreases under a reference-free acceptance predicate. Across five benchmarks spanning logical reasoning (SMT-LIB2), constraint programming (MiniZinc), and planning (PDDL), DRAGO cuts regressions by nearly an order of magnitude, to 1.3%, while improving answer accuracy by 12.9 percentage points over zero-shot formalization and 8.7 percentage points over LLM-diagnostic repair, averaged across benchmarks. We also uncover two rendering defects in Planetarium that cause 50% (3,086 instances) of its floor-tile split to be inconsistent with the reference formalizations, and release a corrected split.

selected_evidence.title: FRACTAL: A Self-Similar Multi-Agent Orchestration Architecture with Formal Communication, Convergence, and Depth Bounds
selected_evidence.text: Abstract: We present FRACTAL, a self-similar multi-agent architecture for recursive goal decomposition, in which the same five-component organizational pattern -- Orchestrator, Ensemble, Knowledge Ledger, Decision Maker, Meta-Observer -- recurs at every level of a decomposition tree. We make four formal contributions: (1) a communication bound showing intra-node cost is linear in ensemble size and round count (O(kr)) under a two-phase blind-proposal/stress-test protocol, versus quadratic cost for free-form debate, with an explicit, stated assumption on fixed evaluator count; (2) a two-mode orchestration criterion separating generative and evaluative phases via a measurable diversity-saturation threshold; (3) a supermajority convergence guarantee with explicit probability bounds at stated agreement levels, and a formal depth bound under an operationalized goal-complexity measure; (4) a Bayesian inter-layer escalation mechanism unifying hysteresis and contract-breach signaling under one posterior update. We illustrate the architecture's execution qualitatively on a worked example and a multi-layer case study; we do not report quantitative performance claims in this paper, and we explicitly discuss the formal and inductive-bias limitations of the model, including an unimplemented but architecture-compatible direction toward bounded self-improvement. We use "fractal" as an architectural metaphor for self-similarity, not a measured mathematical property. Empirical validation of the architecture's comparative performance is left to future work.

{"id": "f34ad45741b405ff9e69", "title": "Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22466", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-15T17:39:38+00:00", "first_published_at": "2026-10-15T17:39:38+00:00", "announced_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "updated_at": null, "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "time_basis": "feed_announcement", "text": "Abstract: Harness evolution automatically optimizes the prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration code around a fixed-weight model, offering a way to improve agentic systems without updating model weights. brief.title: 评测方法学速览：harness 增益归因、日常推理新基准、agent 规划的语义检验
brief.overview: 本期简报依据所给 arXiv 论文片段与日期元数据整理；三篇论文的公告时间均为 2026-10-19 04:00 UTC，首次提交时间均为 2026-10-15，非今日首次发表。其他来源状态未在所给材料中体现。

items.title: Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution
items.summary: 提出 Harness-Delta Attribution（HDA）评测协议，把「harness 演化」（不改模型权重，只迭代优化 prompt、工具、编排代码）带来的搜索集增益拆为三部分：伪影驱动的过拟合、可由测试时算力扩张解释的增益、以及余下的残差（作为可泛化改进的上界）。实验覆盖 11 个执行模型、3 个 harness 演化框架，任务含数学、代码、创造性与 agentic 四类；在 21 个搜索集增益统计显著的设置中，过拟合与测试时扩展平均分别解释 54% 和 14% 的增益，二者合计在 14 个设置中超过 50%。搜索集增益常无法迁移到留出任务，且基于验证集的选择信号不足以阻止过拟合。arXiv 首次提交 2026-10-15，今日为 RSS 公告。
items.why_it_matters: 你关注的 benchmark 与 evaluation 正好是这篇的攻击面：如果团队用「改 prompt/脚手架后分数涨了」来汇报，HDA 提供了可直接借用的归因协议和过拟合上界估计口径，也提醒验证集分数不等于泛化。

items.title: Testing the Planning Claims of LLM-Based Agents against Formal Semantics
items.summary: 用形式语义检验 LLM agent 的「规划」主张：任务以自然语言给出，但每个任务背后绑定一个隐藏 PDDL 模型，由它判定每个动作是否适用、目标是否达成、以及任务是否可解，从而不依赖端到端成功率或 LLM 裁判。实验横跨 5 个域（其中 2 个为本文新增，随论文发布）、4 个模型、6 种提示策略、3 种 agent 架构：最佳配置离线解出 78% 的可解任务，在线仅 40%（agent 多数情况下未检查状态就行动）；不可解任务在不到 10% 的 episode 中被识别；更重的提示策略 token 消耗是直接提示的 5 至 22 倍且无清晰收益；性能在模型间的差异大于在提示策略或架构间的差异。arXiv 首次提交 2026-10-15，今日为公告。
items.why_it_matters: 结论直接冲击「用成功率或 LLM judge 证明 agent 会规划」的评测惯例：你若要评审或设计 agent 评测，可参考其中「隐藏形式语义 + 逐步动作可验证性」的设计，把不可解任务的识别率单列为指标。

items.title: Are Large Reasoning Models Good Everyday Reasoners? A Comparison with Non-Reasoning Models on Logical Reasoning Tasks
items.summary: 构建基于语言与语用推理现象的基准，在受控提示条件下比较大型推理模型（LRM）与非推理模型的日常逻辑推理表现。主要发现：(1) 当日常推理偏离教科书式形式逻辑规则时，推理模型表现下降；(2) 部分非推理模型在 chain-of-thought 提示下超过同等推理模型；(3) 追加指令对推理行为的控制力有限。作者据此认为当前推理模型未可靠掌握日常推理，后训练目标与评测维度需扩展。论文给出的是定性方向性结论，摘要未披露具体模型清单与分数。arXiv 首次提交 2026-10-15，今日为公告。
items.why_it_matters: 对你来说是现成可复用的新评测维度：若你的 benchmark 集偏数理与形式逻辑，这篇提示了「偏离形式规则」的语用推理场景会系统性压低推理模型分数，也适合作为检验 CoT/指令控制是否真有效的对照设置。

selected_evidence.title: Are Large Reasoning Models Good Everyday Reasoners? A Comparison with Non-Reasoning Models on Logical Reasoning Tasks
selected_evidence.text: Abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) that leverage test-time computation achieve strong performance on mathematical and scientific benchmarks and are increasingly deployed in real-world applications. However, their ability to perform \textit{everyday logical reasoning}, which often departs from textbook formal logic, remains underexplored. In this work, we systematically evaluate how well reasoning models align with everyday reasoning patterns by introducing a benchmark based on linguistic and pragmatic reasoning phenomena. We also compare reasoning models with non-reasoning models under controlled prompting conditions. We find that, in many cases, (1) reasoning models show degraded performance in everyday reasoning when such reasoning deviates from formal logical rules, (2) some non-reasoning models with chain-of-thought prompting outperform comparable reasoning models in everyday reasoning, and (3) prompting with additional instructions provides limited control over reasoning behavior. These findings suggest that current reasoning models do not reliably capture everyday reasoning and point to limitations in post-training, motivating improved training objectives and evaluation across diverse forms of reasoning.

selected_evidence.title: Testing the Planning Claims of LLM-Based Agents against Formal Semantics
selected_evidence.text: Abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly credited with the competences of practical reasoning: planning, monitoring, and correcting their own actions. Their success is attributed to the prompting strategies and agent architectures built around the model, such as chain-of-thought, search-based prompting, self-refinement, reflection, critics and tool-using loops. Yet these claims are usually supported by end-to-end success rates, which show only whether a task was completed, or by LLM judges, which are not verifiers. We test LLM planning against formal semantics. Tasks are posed in natural language, but each is grounded in a hidden PDDL model that decides whether every action is applicable, whether the goal is reached, and whether a plan exists at all. Across five domains (two of them new, all released with the paper), four models, six prompting strategies and three agent architectures, the best configuration solves 78% of the solvable tasks offline but only 40% online, where agents mostly act without inspecting the state. Unsolvable tasks are recognised in under 10% of episodes, and heavier prompting strategies use 5 to 22 times as many tokens as direct prompting with no clear gain. In our experiments, planning performance varied more across models than across prompting strategies or agent architectures. Claims that agents can plan require evidence from validated action traces.

selected_evidence.title: Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution
selected_evidence.text: Abstract: Harness evolution automatically optimizes the prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration code around a fixed-weight model, offering a way to improve agentic systems without updating model weights. The agent harness is iteratively optimized to achieve higher performance on the search set. But how much of this gain reflects benchmark-specific overfitting or additional inference-time compute, and how much may generalize beyond the search set? In this work, we introduce Harness-Delta Attribution (HDA), an evaluation protocol that dissects an evolution gain into artifact-driven overfitting, gains explained by test-time scaling, and the remainder, which gives an upper bound on residual generalizable improvement. We apply HDA to 11 executor models and three harness-evolution frameworks across math, coding, creativity, and agentic tasks. In 21 of these settings that show statistically significant search-set gains, we find that a large share of the improvement is explained by overfitting or test-time scaling. Specifically, among these 21 settings, overfitting and test-time scaling account for 54% and 14% of the gain on average; their combined share exceeds 50% in 14 settings. The residual and held-out transfer vary substantially across tasks, models, and frameworks. Importantly, search-set gains often fail to transfer to held-out tasks, and provide limited evidence that they will persist under practical distribution shifts. Moreover, validation-based signals are insufficient to prevent overfitting. These results motivate attribution-aware evaluation in future harness evolution research.
